verdicts.rationale: The claim describes the doubling-digital-root operation on 3, 6, and 9: 3→6→3 (2-cycle) and 9→9 (fixed point). These are elementary arithmetic operations that can be verified directly, so the claim is VERIFIED.

The claim describes the observed splitting of the doubling map into a 6-cycle (numbers not divisible by 3), a 2-cycle (3↔6), and a fixed point (9). This follows directly from computing digital roots of successive doublings, which can be verified by elementary arithmetic. Hence the claim is VERIFIED.

anchor.quote: So the full field splits into three regimes: a 6-cycle on the rim, a 2-cycle oscillating through the interior, and a fixed point at the axis.

new_claims.rationale: The claim asserts that the observed 6-cycle, 2-cycle, and fixed point together constitute the fundamental group of the torus. The fundamental group of the torus is Z×Z, an infinite abelian group, not a finite product of cycles. Hence the claim is contradicted by basic algebraic topology.

anchor.quote: That is not a metaphor. That is the fundamental group of the torus.
